independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Independent re-derivation, OL lens. NUMBERING: web_mt_offset_map.json gives Ps 105 rule identity (45 WEB / 45 MT verses), so the row's 1:1 pairings web:Ps.105.42 = oshb:Ps.105.42 through web:Ps.105.45 = oshb:Ps.105.45 are arithmetically correct; citation_sweep.py returns status GREEN with 0 problems, 0 prose-pair problems and 0 prose dual-cite warns. check_tiling.py over Ps.105.42-Ps.105.45 covers 4 of 4 verses with 0 gaps and 0 overlaps; check_refs_mirror.py, check_marks.py, check_language_zones.py and check_universals.py each return 0 flags. HEBREW: I re-spliced the row's Hebrew runs from verse_map_oshb.json and ran collate.py in batch; 5 of 5 runs reach BYTE tier against the ref they bind to - the v42 quote and both bare causal-particle runs against oshb:Ps.105.42, the psalm-final frame quote in the rationale and in device_notes against oshb:Ps.105.45. No hand-typing and no shell transit of pointed text. MARKS: pmarks_Ps.json shows no selah anywhere in Ps 105, and the psalm's 2 ketiv/qere notes sit at oshb:Ps.105.18 and oshb:Ps.105.28, both outside the span, so the row's silence on disclosure objects is correct; the 1 paseq recorded at MT 105:45 is seg-layer, single-witness, and is not claimed. WEB FIDELITY: 4 of 4 curly-quoted spans in the rationale reproduce their cited WEB verses letter-for-letter. SEAM: the row's warrant rests on the causal particle opening 105:42 and on the covenant-memory echo of 105:8-9. Both are byte-real: MT 105:8 opens זָכַ֣ר לְעוֹלָ֣ם בְּרִית֑וֹ (oshb:Ps.105.8) and MT 105:9 carries אֶת אַבְרָהָ֑ם (oshb:Ps.105.9), which the span's opening line answers with כִּֽי זָ֭כַר אֶת דְּבַ֣ר קָדְשׁ֑וֹ (oshb:Ps.105.42). A serious rival I could build is that a causal clause normally grounds what PRECEDES it, which would attach 105:42 backward to the wilderness sequence 105:37-41 and move the seam to 105:42|43. Byte evidence defeats that rival: the opening address at MT 105:6 is the bicolon זֶ֭רַע אַבְרָהָ֣ם עַבְדּ֑וֹ בְּנֵ֖י יַעֲקֹ֣ב בְּחִירָֽיו (oshb:Ps.105.6), and its two halves are redistributed across the row's opening pair of verses - אֶֽת אַבְרָהָ֥ם עַבְדּֽוֹ (oshb:Ps.105.42) answers the opening colon and אֶת בְּחִירָֽיו (oshb:Ps.105.43) answers the closing colon. Skeleton sweeps confirm the pairing is confined to this psalm: the servant-of-Abraham collocation returns 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Ps.105.6, oshb:Ps.105.42) and the chosen-ones form returns 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Ps.105.6, oshb:Ps.105.43), unit VERSES in both sweeps. 105:42 and 105:43 therefore belong to one inclusio arm and cannot be prised apart at the rival seam; the row's span start and its rejected_alternative reasoning survive. The close is equally firm: MT 105:45 ends on the pointed frame form הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ (oshb:Ps.105.45), which the device inventory records as verse-final, and the psalm boundary follows. unit_type strophe and confidence high are both calibrated on that evidence, so I do not contest the span, the parent, or the typology. DEFECTS: two, both in evidence form rather than in the segmentation - see challenges. OBSERVATIONS not filed as challenges: (a) device_notes asserts a fact about Psalm 104's close that no boundary_evidence_refs entry covers; the fact is true (oshb:Ps.104.35 carries the same pointed frame form at byte tier), the mention is psalm-level rather than verse-level so check_refs_mirror.py cannot see it, and device_notes disclaims the comparison as texture, so I leave it as an observation; (b) the row's 2-letter pointed particle runs sit in fields lacking an oshb: ref, but citation_sweep.py's Hebrew-binding arm has a 3-letter floor and Ps 105 is an identity psalm, so the bare verse pointers resolve without ambiguity - a toolkit threshold artifact, not a row defect.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative presents a stitched composite that does not reproduce WEB text inside curly double quotes, in a field lacking any web: ref, breaching the mandatory curly-quote-plus-inline-web-ref convention and enclosing a connective that WEB does not carry.
challenges.evidence: check_web_quotes.py on this row flags 1 of 5 quoted spans checked: path [0].rejected_alternative, refs_nearby [], issue 'curly quote with NO web: ref in its field' - the field carries just the bare pointers '105:42' and '105:43-45'. The flagged span is also not WEB text. Reproducing it in straight quotes: 'for he remembered… [therefore] he brought his people out… that they might keep'. web_quote_found() against the WEB texts of web:Ps.105.41 through web:Ps.105.45 returns False for the composite and for 2 of its 3 segments, because WEB capitalises both sentence openings - “For he remembered his holy word, and Abraham, his servant.” (web:Ps.105.42) and “He brought his people out with joy, his chosen with singing.” (web:Ps.105.43) - while the bracketed connective 'therefore' is absent from the span: 0 of 5 WEB verses (web:Ps.105.41-Ps.105.45) contain it, against 34 verses book-wide. The third segment, “that they might keep” (web:Ps.105.45), is the 1 segment that does verbatim-match. Under the book-wide convention that curly double quotes are reserved for WEB text and must sit beside an inline web: ref in the same field, this field needs a recut: straight-quoted paraphrase with the connective outside the quotation, or 3 separately-quoted spans reproduced letter-for-letter, with a web: ref beside them.

challenges.claim: device_notes puts the hallelu-Yah frame at 25 book-wide occurrences by folding the inventory's 'other' entry at MT 115:17 into the frame as an interior position, but that token is a prefixed imperfect verb plus the divine short name, so the frame proper is 24 verses.
challenges.evidence: Swept object, declared before the count: the imperative praise-formula as a SPELLING, spliced from source bytes at oshb:Ps.105.45. A byte-tier sweep of that pointed string הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ (oshb:Ps.105.45) returns 13 verses book-wide, unit VERSES - precisely the inventory's verse_final list, which includes oshb:Ps.104.35 and oshb:Ps.105.45, so the row's Ps 104 comparison is itself sound at byte tier. A skeleton sweep of the same string returns 26 verses and 26 token occurrences book-wide. Subtracting the inventory's 11 verse-initial plus 13 verse-final leaves 2 residue verses, and they are the 2 documented skeleton collisions: web:Ps.22.26 = oshb:Ps.22.27, and web:Ps.115.17 = oshb:Ps.115.17, whose text reads יְהַֽלְלוּ יָ֑הּ (oshb:Ps.115.17) - a prefixed imperfect verb governing the divine short name, glossed by WEB as “The dead don’t praise Yah, nor any who go down into silence,” (web:Ps.115.17), which is not an instance of the imperative frame. The inventory files that verse under the bucket it names 'other', and it is the 1 member of that bucket. The frame proper therefore totals 11 + 13 = 24 verses, so the device_notes figure of 25 relabels a collision as a frame position and overstates the frame by 1. The repair is an arithmetic recut to 24 frame verses with the 115:17 collision named as such, and it leaves the row's membership claim for oshb:Ps.105.45 untouched.
